title: Regular pullback of a divisorial log regular pair
statement: Let $g:Y\to X$ be a regular morphism of locally Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres (each fibre remains regular after every finite extension of its residue field). Let $B\subset X$ be a nowhere dense closed subset for which $(X,B)$ is a divisorial fine saturated log regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. Then $g^{-1}B$ is nowhere dense and $(Y,g^{-1}B)$ is a divisorial fine saturated log regular pair. More precisely, the inverse-image log structure $g^*M_X$ is log regular, its triviality locus is $g^{-1}(X\setminus B)$, and its structural map identifies it with $\mathcal O_Y\cap j_*\mathcal O_{Y\setminus g^{-1}B}^{\times}$, where $j:Y\setminus g^{-1}B\hookrightarrow Y$ is the open inclusion. Here the inverse-image log structure is the log structure associated to the prelog monoid sheaf $g^{-1}M_X\to\mathcal O_Y$; equivalently it adjoins the units of $\mathcal O_Y$ to that prelog monoid and identifies its already invertible elements with these units. Empty boundary and empty source are allowed.

source.place: Expose VI 1.2--1.4, printed p.69, and the regular-completion pullback in VII 3.2, printed p.82, with the log-regular version obtained from the stratum definition. Local algebra: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 031E (lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre) and Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total). The flat local dimension formulas for the chart ideal and its quotient give the same characteristic rank; VI 1.4 identifies the resulting log structure with the divisorial one.

proof.text: Put $H=g^{-1}M_X$, with its prelog map $a:H\to\mathcal O_Y$ (a natural monoid homomorphism of sheaves on the small etale site of the locally Noetherian scheme $Y$). For etale $V\to Y$ put $B_V=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, $E_V=a_V^{-1}(B_V^\times)$, and let $P(V)=H(V)\oplus_{E_V}B_V^\times$ be the presheaf pushout with $[m,u]\mapsto a_V(m)u$. Working in a universe containing the site data, let $\eta:P\to N=P^\#$ be its commutative-monoid sheafification [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification]. By [lem-trf-prelog-pushout-log-axiom], $N$ with the induced structural map is a log structure [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], with natural maps $i:H\to N$, $j:\mathcal O_Y^\times\to N$ satisfying $\eta_V([m,u])=i_V(m)j_V(u)$. By [lem-trf-prelog-pushout-hom-extension], composition with $i$ is a bijection from log-structure maps $N\to K$ to compatible maps $H\to K$, for every log structure $K$ on $Y$. Thus this explicit $N$ is exactly the associated log structure $g^*M_X$ of the statement, not an arbitrarily chosen structure.

source.place: VI 1.1 (associated-log convention); explicit pushout construction and its elementary universal-property verification

proof.text: Fix $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, put $\bar x=g\bar y$, and write $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $C=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$. By [lem-per-regular-geometric-stalk-map] the canonical $h:A\to C$ is local and flat between Noetherian local rings and $F=C/\mathfrak m_A C$ is regular local. The inverse-image stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies $H_{\bar y}$ with $(M_X)_{\bar x}$. The underlying-set clause of monoid sheafification and [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheafification-geometric-stalk] identify the stalk of $N$ with the stalk of the presheaf pushout. Explicitly a pair of germs, an inverse witnessing invertibility, and any finite chain of defining congruence relations are all represented on one common pointed neighbourhood; hence taking these filtered germs commutes with this pushout. Since a local ring map reflects units, $a(m)$ is invertible in $C$ exactly when its image in $A$ is invertible. The log axiom on $M_X$ therefore gives the canonical formula $N_{\bar y}=(M_X)_{\bar x}\oplus_{A^\times}C^\times$, compatibly with structure maps.

source.place: Geometric-stalk construction and inverse-image formula, Tags 03PT and 04HX; strict-local algebra as isolated in the cited new node

proof.text: An fs chart $Q\to M_X|_W$ on an etale neighbourhood $W\to X$ pulls back to a map $Q\to N|_T$ on $T=Y\times_XW$, which is etale over $Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. For every geometric point of $T$, write $A,C$ for the corresponding geometric local rings of $W,T$ and $E_Q=\beta^{-1}(A^\times)\subset Q$. The chart formula in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and step 2 give $(Q\oplus_{E_Q}A^\times)\oplus_{A^\times}C^\times=Q\oplus_{E_Q}C^\times$: the maps send $[[q,a],c]$ to $[q,h(a)c]$ and $[q,c]$ to $[[q,1],c]$. They respect the defining relations and are inverse. Locality gives $E_Q=(h\beta)^{-1}(C^\times)$. Thus $Q\to N|_T$ is a chart by the stalkwise chart definition. Every $\bar y$ has such a pointed neighbourhood by choosing a chart at $g\bar y$ and taking the lifted pair $(\bar y,\bar w)$ in the fibre product. Hence $N$ is fs. This argument uses only the stalk formula (valid for any scheme morphism with local stalk maps), not an assertion that this etale chart map is regular.

source.place: VI 1.1: fs charts; elementary associativity of the displayed pushouts

proof.text: At the fixed $\bar x$, choose the sharp chart $P=\overline M_{X,\bar x}$ supplied by [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart]. In this chart the elements mapping to $A^\times$ are precisely $0\in P$: their classes in the identified characteristic are zero, and $P$ is sharp. The chart definition therefore gives $(M_X)_{\bar x}=P\oplus A^\times$, and step 2 gives $N_{\bar y}=P\oplus C^\times$. Their quotients by the unit groups are both $P$, so their group-completion ranks agree, say $r$. Write $a(p)\in A$ for the chart functions and $I=(a(p):p\ne0)\subset A$. Locality of $h$ shows each $h(a(p))$ remains a nonunit, and multiplication by arbitrary units does not change the ideal generated by these elements. Thus the ideal of nonunits of $N_{\bar y}$ is exactly $J=IC$. By the log-regular-pair hypothesis and [def-trf-log-regular-pair], $A/I$ is regular local and $\dim A=\dim(A/I)+r$.

source.place: VI 1.2 (log regularity on the strict-local stratum) and VI 1.6 (sharp chart)

proof.text: The quotient map $A/I\to C/J$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat], applied to the flat $A$-module $C$ and $J=IC$. Both quotients are Noetherian local rings, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A/I$ and $\mathfrak m_C/J$, and the map is local. Here $I\subset\mathfrak m_A$, $J\subset\mathfrak m_C$, since the chart generators are nonunits. Its closed fibre is $(C/J)/(\mathfrak m_A/I)(C/J)=C/\mathfrak m_A C=F$. The base $A/I$ is regular by step 4 and $F$ is regular by step 2. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre] implies that $C/J$ is regular local.

source.place: Tags 00HI (flat quotient base change) and 031E (flat over regular with regular closed fibre)

proof.text: Apply the local dimension formula [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to $A\to C$ and to $A/I\to C/J$ at their maximal ideals; all four rings are Noetherian, both maps are flat and local, and both closed fibres are the same $F$ by steps 2 and 5. It gives $\dim C=\dim A+\dim F$ and $\dim(C/J)=\dim(A/I)+\dim F$. Substituting $\dim A=\dim(A/I)+r$ from step 4 and commuting the two summands yields $\dim C=\dim(C/J)+r$. Together with step 5 and the characteristic identification of step 4, these are precisely the log-regularity conditions at $\bar y$ in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Since $\bar y$ was arbitrary, $(Y,N)$ is log regular.

source.place: Tag 00ON, local dimension formula; ILO VI 1.2 for the log-regularity criterion

proof.text: The characteristic calculation in step 4 shows that the triviality locus of $N$ is $V=g^{-1}(X\setminus B)$, because the divisorial pair in [def-trf-log-regular-pair] has triviality locus exactly $X\setminus B$. Apply [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure] to the locally Noetherian fs log regular scheme $(Y,N)$ obtained above: $V$ is open dense and the structural map identifies $N$ with $\mathcal O_Y\cap j_*\mathcal O_V^\times$. Its complement is the closed subset $g^{-1}B$; being the complement of an open dense subset it has empty interior and is nowhere dense. This is the divisorial fs log regular pair required by [def-trf-log-regular-pair], with the specified structural identification. If $Y$ is empty, all stalk conditions are vacuous and the empty open is dense. If $B$ is empty, every $P$ is zero and the same argument gives $N=\mathcal O_Y^\times$ and regularity of $Y$; no positive rank or nonempty boundary was used.

source.place: VI 1.4, printed p.69: dense triviality locus and divisorial identification

lean.statement: theorem logRegularPair_regularPullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (g : Y ⟶ X) [Flat g] (hg : ∀ (x : X) (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (X.residueField x) K] [Module.Finite (X.residueField x) K], IsRegularScheme (pullback (g.fiberToSpecResidueField x) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (X.residueField x) K))))) (U : X.Opens) (hU : DenseRange U.ι) (hpair : IsDivisorialFineSaturatedLogRegularPair X U.toScheme U.ι hU) : ∃ hV : DenseRange (g ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι, IsDivisorialFineSaturatedLogRegularPair Y (g ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme (g ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι hV ∧ ∃ (MX : EtaleLogStructure X) (MY : EtaleLogStructure Y) (fsX : MX.IsFineSaturated) (fsY : MY.IsFineSaturated) (eX : MX.monoidSheaf.obj ≅ divisorialLogPresheaf U.ι) (eY : MY.monoidSheaf.obj ≅ divisorialLogPresheaf (g ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι) (f : EtaleLogHom ⟨Y, inferInstance, MY, fsY⟩ ⟨X, inferInstance, MX, fsX⟩), eX.hom ≫ divisorialStructuralMap U.ι = MX.alpha ∧ eY.hom ≫ divisorialStructuralMap (g ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι = MY.alpha ∧ f.base = g ∧ f.IsStrict ∧ (FineSaturatedLogScheme.mk Y inferInstance MY fsY).IsLogRegular ∧ MY.trivialityLocus = (g ⁻¹ᵁ U : Set Y)
lean.note: The closed boundary is encoded by the complement of the open U. DenseRange of the inverse-image open inclusion is exactly nowhere density of the pulled-back closed boundary. The existential log structures are identified with the prescribed divisorial presheaves via isomorphisms commuting with alpha. The log morphism has base g and the recorded graph-normalized IsStrict property, which identifies MY with the associated inverse-image of MX, including its canonical map. reviewed_lean.note: Clause by clause, the theorem says what the node says. Flat g; every fibre regular after every finite extension of the residue field (including the trivial one), which is exactly geometric regularity. The boundary is the complement of a dense open U, and hpair is the recorded pair predicate.
